items.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But then I liked Red Garland, and I like Wynton Kelly, Phineas Newborn, Jr.

ctx.x: No doubt, the Modern Jazz Quartet. I think the reason was because of John Lewis and the classical thing, and Milt Jackson and the blues. So, there it is, classical and gospel. Milt Jackson, gospel, right? So that was just a natural. But then, Oscar Peterson. Oscar Peterson beat me up. Whoa. It’s like getting on a bronco. I’m trying to hold on. I’m not even playing, but this guy – not only is he playing with such clean technique, but he’s swinging so hard at any tempo. A medium tempo, there he goes. A tempo that…

took me a while to get into Bud Powell and even longer to get into Thelonious Monk. In those early days, I guess I’m talking about the romantic piano players. Erroll Garner, George Shearing, Billy Taylor. But then I liked Red Garland, and I like Wynton Kelly, Phineas Newborn, Jr. There were some that didn’t have their own big name, but – Bill Evans.
Ahmad Jamal was already working in this area as well.
